{{short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Pete explaining a proof.jpg|thumb|Peter G. Casazza discussing the core structures of Grassmannian frames in a classroom he and his wife, Janet Tremain, installed in the basement of their home.  Photo taken May 15, 2017.]]

[[File:Peter Casazza in Hong Kong.jpg|thumb|Peter G. Casazza along with some of his fellow coauthors during a math workshop in Hong Kong.  From left to right: Bernhard G. Bodmann, John I. Haas IV, Peter G. Casazza, and Janet Tremain (his wife).]]

'''Peter G. Casazza''' (June 28, 1945 - October 26, 2025) born in [[Albany, New York]], was an American mathematician who worked at the [[University of Missouri]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Casazza|first1=Peter|title=Departmental Webpage|url=https://faculty.missouri.edu/~casazzap/|access-date=2017-04-10|archive-date=2020-01-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200101153208/http://faculty.missouri.edu/~casazzap/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He began his career as a [[Banach space]] theorist,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casazza|first1=Peter G.|title=The Norms of Projections Onto Ideals in the Disk Algebra|journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society|date=November 1992|volume=24|issue=6|pages=552–558|doi=10.1112/blms/24.6.552}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casazza|first1=Peter|title=Complete Bases and Normal Structure in Banach Spaces|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society |date=February 1972|volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=443–447 |doi=10.2307/2039175|jstor=2039175|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casazza|first1=P. G.|last2=Jarchow|first2=H.|title=Self-induced compactness in Banach spaces|journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh, Section A|date=14 November 2011|volume=126|issue=2|pages=355–362|doi=10.1017/S0308210500022770|arxiv=math/9403210|s2cid=119164575}}</ref> but he was perhaps most well known for his role in the development of [[frame (linear algebra)]] theory as a popular discipline of mathematical research.<ref>{{cite book|editor1=Peter G. Casazza|editor2= Gitta Kutyniok|editor2-link=Gitta Kutyniok|title=Finite frames : theory and applications|date=2013|publisher=Birkhäuser|location=Berlin|isbn=978-0-8176-8372-6}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casazza|first1=Peter G.|last2=Pinkham|first2=Eric|last3=Tuomanen|first3=Brian|title=Riesz outer product Hilbert space frames: Quantitative bounds, topological properties, and full geometric characterization|journal=Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications|date=September 2016|volume=441|issue=1|pages=475–498|doi=10.1016/j.jmaa.2016.04.001|arxiv=1410.7755|s2cid=14173332}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bodmann|first1=Bernhard G.|last2=Casazza|first2=Peter G.|last3=Paulsen|first3=Vern I.|last4=Speegle|first4=Darrin|title=Spanning and independence properties of frame partitions|journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|date=1 July 2012|volume=140|issue=7|pages=2193–2207|doi=10.1090/S0002-9939-2011-11072-4|arxiv=1004.2446|s2cid=33897848}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Bodmann|first1=Bernhard G.|last2=Casazza|first2=Peter G.|last3=Kutyniok|first3=Gitta|author3-link=Gitta Kutyniok|title=A quantitative notion of redundancy for finite frames|journal=Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis|date=May 2011|volume=30|issue=3|pages=348–362|doi=10.1016/j.acha.2010.09.004|arxiv=0910.5904|s2cid=15700141}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casazza|first1=P. G.|last2=Tremain|first2=J. C.|title=The Kadison-Singer Problem in mathematics and engineering|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=3 February 2006|volume=103|issue=7|pages=2032–2039|doi=10.1073/pnas.0507888103|pmid=16461465|pmc=1413700|arxiv=math/0510024|bibcode=2006PNAS..103.2032C|doi-access=free}}</ref> He earned his Ph.D. in mathematics from the University of Iowa in 1972 and held appointments at the University of Alabama-Huntsville before joining the University of Missouri-Columbia in 1983 where he stayed until his retirement in 2021.  He also held visiting appointments around the world, including at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in Israel, the University of Cambridge in England, and Odense University in Denmark.

Peter Casazza has over 100 publications,<ref>{{cite web|title=Peter G. Casazza (University of Missouri, Columbia) on ResearchGate - Expertise: Applied Mathematics, Analysis, Statistics|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Peter_Casazza2|website=www.researchgate.net|language=en}}</ref> several of which are coauthored with his wife, Janet Tremain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Peter G. Casazza (University of Missouri, Columbia) on ResearchGate - Expertise: Applied Mathematics, Analysis, Statistics|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Peter_Casazza2|website=www.researchgate.net|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casazza|first1=P. G.|last2=Tremain|first2=J. C.|title=The Kadison-Singer Problem in mathematics and engineering|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|date=3 February 2006|volume=103|issue=7|pages=2032–2039|doi=10.1073/pnas.0507888103|pmid=16461465|pmc=1413700|arxiv=math/0510024|bibcode=2006PNAS..103.2032C|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He was an active mathematical researcher and directed the Frame Research Center in [[Columbia, Missouri]].
